production.note: Customer production began September 9, 2019 in Zuffenhausen. End year is for the pre-facelift car and is inferred: Porsche announced the updated 2025 Taycan on February 6, 2024 with US arrival in summer 2024 (https://newsroom.porsche.com/en_US/2024/products/02062024_The_new_2025-_Porsche_Taycan_models.html); no source stating the exact last build date of the original car was found.

configuration.note: Two permanently excited synchronous motors, one per axle.

transmission.note: Two-speed automatic gearbox on the rear axle; the front axle uses a single-speed gear set.

powerHp.note: Peak output with overboost and Launch Control: 'up to 750 horsepower (560 kW)'. Without overboost the Turbo S is rated 616 hp (460 kW) per Porsche's US technical spec sheet.

weightLb.note: Launch (model year 2020) US curb weight; single configuration. Porsche's US spec sheet for model year 2021 lists 5,101 lb - see discrepancies.

discrepancies.reason: Model year: 5,121 lb is quoted for the 2020 launch car, 5,101 lb is on Porsche's US spec sheet for model year 2021. (The EU DIN figure, 2,295 kg, is a different market and standard.)
discrepancies.resolution: Used 5,121 lb to match the 2020 reference model year. It rests on two non-manufacturer sources; the manufacturer's 2021 sheet is 20 lb lower.

discrepancies.reason: Rounding of the 560 kW overboost figure (560 kW = 750.97 hp). Porsche's US material states 750 hp.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 750 hp, the manufacturer's US figure.
